The recommendation

Skip the hype. Go to Stanhill.

For families starting in South-East London, it offers the strongest balance of journey, authentic farm atmosphere and value. Saturday 17 October adds just enough toddler-friendly fun without turning the day into a theme-park spend.

£7.50walk-in group up to 8
Dartfordtrain, then bus or taxi
17 Octbest day to go

Three choices that fit a family day

Ranked for public transport from South-East London, value, authentic farm feel and what works well with a toddler.

Saturday 17 October

The sweet spot for 2026

Earlier than half-term crowds, late enough for full autumn atmosphere, and one of Stanhill’s selected activity days. Sunday 18 October is the calmer fallback.

1 · Best overallWilmington, Kent

Stanhill Farm

A real farm, a short transfer from Dartford, and an unusually fair group ticket. The right answer unless heavy rain makes the field impractical.

Entry£7.50 / group of 8
Final legDartford + bus/taxi
17 Oct extrasRides, face paint, toast
Pumpkins£1.50–£15
  • Strawed patch is the pram-friendly choice; main field may be muddy.
  • Only portaloo toilets, but the disabled portaloo has baby changing.
  • Weekend tickets sell out; walk-ins can be refused.

2 · Best underratedSouth Nutfield

Priory Farm Estate

The best upgrade when the tractor ride matters more than saving money: 12 acres, a hay maze and enough toddler interest without becoming a theme park.

Entry£9 pp + fee
Final legRedhill + bus/taxi
  • All visitors aged 1+ pay; pumpkins are extra.
  • Tractor and trailer, sand pit and marshmallow roasting.
  • Book online; on-door access depends on availability.

3 · Rainy-day fallbackGodstone, Surrey

Godstone Farm

The facilities-first option: animals, large soft play, toddler zones and a Halloween programme. Better in poor weather, but much less authentic and far pricier.

Base entryFrom £16.95 age 2+
Final legOxted + bus/taxi

  • Base price is £16.95 for age 2+; online savings may apply.
  • Halloween uplift and inclusion details were not verified.

Why Stanhill wins

Spend on pumpkins, not admission.

One £7.50 walk-in ticket admits a group of up to eight. Wheelbarrows are included, all pumpkins are grown on site, and the Dartford connection keeps the final leg manageable with a toddler.

£7.50entry per walk-in group
£39full wheelbarrow option
4.7/5Tripadvisor rating cited

Tulleys looks great. It is the wrong trade-off.

Huge scale and polished photo sets, but entry buys access rather than pumpkins. With the longest journey in this comparison, add-on rides and repeated “overhyped” value complaints, it loses on every priority except spectacle.

A realistic Stanhill day

A flexible sequence for Saturday 17 October. Check a journey planner from your South-East London starting point and match it to the booked arrival window.

Pack for a field, not a feed.

✓
Wellies + layersMain field can be muddy.
✓
Strong carrier bagsThe farm says bin liners are not strong enough.
✓
Pram strategyUse the strawed patch rather than the main field.
✓
Cash + cardUseful for external rides and extras.
✓
Snack backupCafé has drinks, cakes, pastries and savouries.
Start
Leave South-East London

Allow a little buffer for the change or onward connection.

Rail
Travel to Dartford

Dartford is the practical interchange for the farm’s final leg.

Transfer
Take bus 492 or a taxi

The research found roughly 15–20 minutes by bus or 10–15 minutes by taxi from Dartford.

Arrival
Use the booked arrival window

Collect a wheelbarrow, use the strawed patch and take your time choosing.

Midday
Café + selected-date extras

Face painting, marshmallow toasting and small fairground rides are separately charged.

Return
Head home before the rush

Saturday closing is 15:30. A mid-afternoon return keeps the day toddler-sized.

Rain rule

Stanhill can close if the ground is too wet or waterlogged; the report says refunds are given in that case. Godstone is the stronger all-weather fallback because of soft play and indoor facilities.

Do not leave it to Halloween

Popular sizes become picked over near month-end, while 24–25 October brings half-term demand. 17–18 October is the better balance of stock, atmosphere and crowds.

Transport reality

No dedicated 2026 pumpkin shuttles were found. All final legs use normal buses or taxis, so verify weekend service and pre-book a cab where practical.

Open questions

Hewitts’ exact 2026 £/kg, Crockford’s early-PYO price, Godstone’s Halloween uplift, Willows’ chosen-day price and Garsons’ pumpkin prices were not confirmed.
